description: Reference manifest of the M-QCD campaign (m-qcd/PLAN.md §4.2), written by tools/loop_reference/mqcd_campaign.py manifest from mqcd_campaign.json and the committed fixtures. Per row: process, pyAmpliCol route (restriction, fixed parameters), reference runs (fixture path below tests/fixtures/loop, orders, parameters, points, MadLoop accuracy per point and loop squared split order) and existing references. 'pending' marks a reference not committed yet. The pyAmpliCol request uses the fixture's parameters and fixed_parameters (the MadLoop card values).

conventions.laurent: MadLoop/BLHA C_eps = (4 pi)^eps / Gamma(1 - eps); physical couplings; initial spin/colour average and final identical-particle factor included
conventions.squared_split_orders: QCD^2, QED^2 = summed g_s and e powers of the interfering amplitudes; a loop sector's born_sector is its orders minus the correction step
conventions.madloop_accuracy: MadLoop's own ACC(i) of SLOOPMATRIX_THRES per point and loop squared split order: ONE number over the three Laurent coefficients (madloop_settings.madloop_accuracy_definition), not a per-coefficient relative accuracy. In the quadruple-precision evaluation (madloop_evaluation 'quadruple') 0.0 means its two quadruple-precision evaluations (propagators in original and reversed order) printed identical binary64 values for all three coefficients; that test does not see a systematic error both share (g g > u u~ u u~ points 0, 2, 3: accuracy 0.0, reference outliers named in reference_notes)
conventions.second_provider_outcome: per triggered second provider and point: the strict relative difference |a - b| / max(|a|, |b|) of each coefficient from MadLoop's (the outcome of the §4.1 trigger named in second_provider_trigger)
conventions.batch2_relative_deviation: per point and coefficient: how far the batch-2 MadLoop values (MLStabThres 1e-13, HelicityFilterLevel 2), which this evaluation supersedes, are from the reference (Laurent coefficients relative to max(|a|, |b|, |Born| alpha/(2 pi)))
conventions.per_helicity_reference: per point and helicity configuration (the fixture's per_helicity rows): status, comparison, absolute_scale, born_source and born_double_pole_relative_mismatch as for point_reference; 'absolute' entries (a vanishing helicity, or one suppressed below the point's binary64 condition: printed Born mismatch above 1e-13) compare against absolute_scale = the point's summed |Born| over the configurations
conventions.per_helicity: MadLoop SLOOPMATRIXHEL_THRES: colour average and identical-particle factor, no helicity average; HelConfigs.dat helicity labels
conventions.indexing: rows, points, mu_r, point_labels, point_reference, provider_accuracy_per_sector and madloop_return_codes are aligned lists (row i = point i, 0-based); reference_notes and point_status keys are 0-based row indices; scale_variation's point and copy_of_point are 1-based point numbers (mqcd_campaign.py run --point), its row and copy_of_row the 0-based rows

point_reference.status: 'ok': the row is a reference; 'none': no usable provider reference at this point (reason given), validate it by internal oracles only
point_reference.comparison: 'relative': compare per coefficient relative to the reference value; 'absolute': a Born-zero point (§4.1 S3), compare |value - reference| against the tolerance times absolute_scale = |Born| at row absolute_scale_row (the nearest regular point) for the Born, and times absolute_scale alpha/(2 pi) (F_s of §1.4) for the Laurent coefficients, never dividing by the vanishing Born
point_reference.born_source: which value the row's (and its sectors') 'born' is: 'madloop' = MadLoop's printed Born; 'madloop_double_pole_over_universal_factor' = at madloop_qp_point points, MadLoop's printed Born is its double-precision Born at the binary64 rounding of the point, not at the published point, so the reference Born is its quadruple-precision double pole over universal_double_pole_factor (the printed value is kept as born_madloop_binary64_input / born_binary64_input)
point_reference.madloop_point: the point MadLoop's loop values refer to: the published point (quadruple precision at a madloop_qp_point point), the binary64 rounding of the published point (double precision), or MadLoop's quadruple-precision repair of that rounding (~1e-16 from an exact published point)
point_reference.born_double_pole_relative_mismatch: MadLoop's printed Born (double precision at the binary64 input) against the Born its quadruple-precision double pole implies. At a regular point both are the same Born to its binary64 rounding (~1e-16 .. 1e-15): a mismatch above that scale is a loop defect of the reference, not point sensitivity (C01 point 1 of batch 2: 4.8e-13 from MadLoop's helicity filter, Recola's own relation holding to 1e-15), and the integrity tests refuse it at ok points; at madloop_qp_point points (S1-S3) it is the binary64 condition of the limit point, bounded by the family's stated bound
point_reference.max_sector_double_pole_relative_error: largest violation of the universal double pole over the loop squared split orders (MadLoop's printed values, relative to the point's largest double pole); the merge refuses ok points above its tolerance, the integrity tests ok regular points above max(10 x the sector accuracy, 1e-14). At madloop_qp_point points the reference Born is the double pole over the factor, so the relation holds there by construction for every sector with a Born partner; born_double_pole_relative_mismatch is the falsifiable quantity

conventions.fixture_tolerance: 'tolerance' and 'validation_status' are the references.py merge's provider-agreement check (the G1 2e-8 tolerance); they are not M-QCD acceptance values: m-qcd/PLAN.md §1.4 applies, with each point's 'reference' record

evaluation.description: every point in quadruple precision, chosen by MadLoop's own test: the run's copy of loop_matrix.f bypasses MadLoop's double-precision acceptance (references.py --madloop-quadruple, force_quadruple_stage), so every point goes on to MadLoop's quadruple-precision stage, where its CTModeRun -1 test (two propagator directions, forced on every call) at MLStabThres 1e-13 accepts Ninja or else CutTools, exactly as for a point whose double-precision estimate failed; HelicityFilterLevel = 0 (every helicity configuration computed, no numerical helicity filter); every run starts without filters of earlier runs; a run with a double-precision point is refused
evaluation.reason: m-qcd/PLAN.md §1.4 rule 1 compares DD with the reference at 1e-12 per coefficient. The batch-2 evaluation (MLStabThres 1e-13, rescue only where the double-precision estimate failed) left 209 of 303 points in binary64, whose estimate does not bound a cancelling coefficient (C02 point 0 finite 2.0e-12, D11 point 1 single pole 4.3e-12, A06 point 1 single pole 1.2e-12 against estimates of ~1e-14 or exactly 0), and MadLoop's numerical helicity filter (HelicityFilterLevel 2, ZeroThres 1e-9) zeroed and folded mass-suppressed helicities of the massive-b rows (C01 point 1 finite 3.2e-11 off in both precisions; with HelicityFilterLevel 0 MadLoop = Recola to 1e-15). MadLoop's own quadruple-precision selection is kept: a fixed CTModeRun = 4 (Ninja in quadruple precision, no fallback; references.py --madloop-ctmode, diagnostic) is worse where that test rejects Ninja (g g > t t~ g points 0, 3: double pole 3.1e-11 off the universal relation, CutTools 1e-14; g g > u u~ u u~ points 0, 2, 3: 5.5e-12, CutTools 3.5e-13 .. 1.1e-12) while its CTModeRun = 5 twin agrees to 1e-13; and MLStabThres 1e-20 (with NRotations_DP = 1 to fail every double-precision test) rejects Ninja on a one-ulp difference of its two directions, moving g g > t t~ g point 1 to CutTools (finite 1.1e-12 away)

madloop_settings.madloop_accuracy_definition: MadLoop's own accuracy (CTModeRun = -1, ML5_0_COMPUTE_ACCURACY) is ONE number per squared split order, sum_k |v_k(mode 1) - v_k(mode 2)| / (|sum_k v_k| / 3) over the three Laurent coefficients k: it is not a per-coefficient relative accuracy and does not bound a coefficient much smaller than the others (a cancelling finite part or single pole); the campaign's direction test is per coefficient
madloop_settings.requested_relative_accuracy_reason: only for runs kept from batch 2 (madloop_evaluation mode 'mlstabthres'): MLStabThres 1e-13 with MadLoop's forced stability test and quadruple-precision rescue
madloop_settings.special_points: limit-point runs (S1-S3) at points that are MadLoop's own quadruple-precision projection of their binary64 rounding (supplied_points.py --madloop-qp-point), evaluated like every run
plan_deviations_for_coordinator_ruling: every point in MadLoop's quadruple-precision stage (double-precision acceptance bypassed in the run's loop_matrix.f copy, MLStabThres 1e-13, HelicityFilterLevel = 0) instead of the accurate mode of m-qcd/PLAN.md §4.1 (--madloop-accuracy 1e-11 with MadLoop's rescue): stricter, never looser (reason in evaluation); the three runs kept from batch 2 used MLStabThres 1e-13 (1e-20 for the collinear limit points) and are in quadruple precision at every reference point
